cards.notes: Mirrors ARM-FM paper Figure 6, bottom row: DoorKey 5x5 with a new map each episode, a control case where plain RL learns too. Suite armfm-paper (user, 2026-11-22): the paper's MiniGrid tasks the benchmark lacked, trained by FARM, ARM-FM and no-RM; `train` is false, so the card is not in the counted 60, and `runs.yaml` trains it (1.5M steps). Task text, `expect` and the solving and first wrong plan are those of `base-doorkey`: the first task of `examples/arm-fm/minigrid-doorkey/tasks.json`, the benchmark's own restatement (the authors' mission text stays out of cards: their repository has no licence). Step limit 250 (10 x 5^2); generation prices the machine for it from the card's gym id. wrong-1 is the idle plan: it waits to the step limit.

cards.notes: Mirrors ARM-FM paper Figure 6, top row: DoorKey 5x5 on one fixed map. Fixed-map copy of `armfm-doorkey-5x5`: the same task, `expect` and plans, trained on that card's bundles (`bundle_of`; no paraphrases and no bundle of its own, so generate-suite skips it). `layout: fixed` with `layout_seed` 1 is the existing switch: train-rl resets every training and evaluation episode on that seed, and test-rl judges on it (its test.json says the map does not change); the plans and the trace bank use the same seed. Same world and step limit (250) as the source card, so the machine's pricing matches. `train` is false; `runs.yaml` trains it (1.5M steps).

cards.notes: Mirrors ARM-FM paper Figure 7 and Figure 19 (UnlockToUnlock). Task text: the first task of `experiments/dev/arm-fm/babyai-unlock-to-unlock/tasks.json` (UTU-1), the catalogue's restatement of the released mission; the authors' mission text stays out of cards (their repository has no licence). Environment page: the benchmark copy `experiments/benchmark/envs/babyai-unlock-to-unlock/` (Labeling API included). Order rule (2026-11-21, user): commanded steps in one sentence, joined by commas or "and", keep their written order, and "then" states the last one, so `expect` is one `Existence` per step plus the four `Precedence` clauses of the chain, and the chain with the last `Existence` is the `also_ok` answer, as in `base-unlock-pickup`. The world forces every one of those orders (the page's constraints), so the plans can break only `Existence` clauses. Layout: procedural like every benchmark card; the released ARM-FM labeling hard-codes the colours of layout seed 1, so the paper may have trained on that one map (not verified). The plans name the colours of layout seed 1, the only seed the plans run on (the first door and its key are yellow, the second red): both locked doors face the middle room and a plan step cannot name the door of the held key. Step limit 1080. `train` is false; `runs-5m.yaml` trains it at 5M steps (user D3).
